goal: Lets external tools validate a Bitcoin block via the kernel without maintaining a full UTXO set
Helps miners, light clients, and independent verifiers check a block without running a full node
reviewability: Stale, needs rebase and mergeable state is dirty
The core API shape is still disputed, so the reviewed interface may change before merge
agreement: Multiple concept and approach ACKs plus a thorough code-review ACK, no NACKs (yuvicc, nervana21, w0xlt, ismaelsadeeq)
Design already iterated in response to review, moving from two arrays to a callback (ismaelsadeeq, purpleKarrot)
Unaddressed objection: callback risks nondeterminism and unnecessary copying, proposes alternative container type (ajtowns, purpleKarrot)
Unaddressed objection: whether assumevalid or script-check-skip logic should be forced off in this path, no author reply (nervana21)
Unaddressed objection: missing direct test of ValidateBlock and a full caller-side UTXO set test (optout21)

categories.name: kernel
why: P2 because it delivers a concrete new capability external kernel consumers are already prototyping against
Benefits users building block-validation tooling without a full node, such as rust-bitcoinkernel
Not P1 because the API surface is still actively disputed and may change before it ships

categories.name: validation
why: P3 because it reuses existing consensus logic unchanged rather than altering validation behavior
Marginal impact since it's not consensus-critical, but raises an open correctness question about assumevalid interaction
Benefit is mostly to validation reviewers needing to confirm the new entry point behaves safely
